title: Notation
body_md:
For \(k\ge2\), let \([k]:=\{1,\ldots,k\}\) and \(e_1,\ldots,e_k\) be the standard basis of
\(\mathbb R^k\). 
For positive integers \(b,N\), we write \(b\mid N\) if \(N\) is divisible by \(b\).
For matrices, \(\langle A,B\rangle:=\operatorname{tr}(A^\top B)\),
\(\|A\|_{\max}:=\max_{r,j}|A_{r,j}|\), and
\(\|A\|_{\mathrm{sum}}:=\sum_{r,j}|A_{r,j}|\); we use
\(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\) and \(\|A\|_{\mathrm F}\) for the spectral and Frobenius norms.
For \(W\in\mathbb R^{k\times d}\) with rows \(w_r^\top\), define
\(\|W\|_{\mathrm{row}}:=\|W\|_{2,\infty}:=\max_{r \in [k]}\|w_r\|_2\) as a row norm.
For \(a\in\mathbb R^k\) and \(c\in[k]\), define \(\mathbb{S}_c(a):=e^{a_c}/\sum_{\ell=1}^k e^{a_\ell}\), the \(c\)-th component of the softmax map.
We write \(A^{\odot p}\) for entrywise powers and \(\oslash\) for entrywise division, with \(0/0:=0\).
For nonzero vectors \(u,v\), let \(\angle(u,v)\in[0,\pi]\) denote the angle between \(u\) and \(v\).
Write \(\widehat v:=v/\|v\|_2\) for \(v\neq{\mathbf 0}\).
For random quantities indexed by \(d\), \(o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) denotes a term that converges to zero in probability as \(d\to\infty\).

title: Proof idea
body_md:
The proof proceeds through the implicit biases of the optimizers. RowGD and RowGDM approach row-norm margin solutions, SpecGD and Muon approach spectral-norm margin solutions, and SignGD, Signum, and Adam approach max-norm margin solutions. Here, a \(\psi\)-norm margin solution minimizes \(\psi(W)\) among classifiers with training margin at least one; the formal solution sets are defined in Appendix~\ref{app:deterministic-margin}. Under the Gaussian-cloud model, these three solution sets have the distinct asymptotic classifier structures summarized in Proposition~\ref{prop:limiting-geometry}, and Gaussian pairwise-error bounds convert this geometric separation into the population-accuracy ordering.
Because Theorem~\ref{thm:det-optimizer-accuracy-order-clean} is proven through a uniform comparison over all norm-induced margin solutions approached by the optimizers, it does not require directional convergence of optimizers.

























































\begin{proposition}[Limiting classifier geometry]
\label{prop:limiting-geometry}
Let \(W_t^{\rm opt}\) have rows \((w_{i,t}^{\rm opt})^\top\), and let \(\Theta_t^{\rm opt}:=k^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^k\angle(w_{i,t}^{\rm opt},\mu_i)\) denote the average angle between the class mean and classifier row. 
Let \(M_\mu\in\mathbb R^{k\times d}\) have rows \(\mu_i^\top\), let \(P:=I_k-k^{-1}\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\) and \(r_d:=\min\{k-1,d\}\), and let \(C_\mu:=PM_\mu\) have compact SVD \(U_\mu\Sigma_\mu V_\mu^\top\) and polar factor \(Q_\mu:=U_\mu V_\mu^\top\). Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:gaussian-cloud}, \ref{ass:asymptotic-regime}, \ref{ass:adam-init}, \ref{ass:lr-base}, and~\ref{ass:lr-momentum} hold. Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{\rm RowGD/RowGDM:}\quad&
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\max_i\bigl\|\widehat w_{i,t}^{\rm opt}-\widehat\mu_i\bigr\|_2=o_{\mathbb P}(1),\\
\text{\rm SignGD/Signum/Adam:}\quad&
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\max_i\left\|\widehat w_{i,t}^{\rm opt}-\frac{\operatorname{sign}(\mu_i)}{\sqrt d}\right\|_2=o_{\mathbb P}(1),\\
\text{\rm SpecGD/Muon:}\quad&
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\frac1{r_d}\left\|\frac{PW_t^{\rm opt}}{\|PW_t^{\rm opt}\|_{\rm op}}-Q_\mu\right\|_{\rm F}^2=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\end{aligned}
\]
Moreover, \(\limsup_{t\to\infty}|\Theta_t^{\rm opt}-\theta|=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), where \(\theta=0\) for RowGD/RowGDM and \(\theta=\arccos\sqrt{2/\pi}\) for SignGD/Signum/Adam. 
If the aspect ratio \(\alpha>1\), then \(\theta=\arccos\kappa_{\rm sp}(\alpha)\) for SpecGD/Muon, where \(\kappa_{\rm sp}:(0,\infty)\to(0,1)\) is a positive constant depending only on \(\alpha\).\footnote{Its explicit formula is given in \eqref{eq:app-det-all-aspect-scales}. Numerically, \(\kappa_{\rm sp}(1)\approx0.84883\) and \(\kappa_{\rm sp}(2)\approx0.93280\).}
\end{proposition}

title: Remark
body_md:
Unlike the accuracy comparisons in Section~\ref{sec:main-results}, which hold uniformly over all classifier families that the normalized iterates approach and therefore do not require directional convergence, Theorem~\ref{thm:aniso-dd-ordering} assumes directional convergence for each optimizer.
Related directional-convergence assumptions are common in the implicit-bias literature \citep{gunasekar2018implicit, nacson2019convergence, chizat2020implicit, baek2026implicit}.
Under clean training, conditional on the training data, the limit of \(W_t^{\mathrm{opt}}/\|W_t^{\mathrm{opt}}\|_{\mathrm F}\) is fixed and independent of the test-noise eigenbases, which enter only at test time. 
Hence, the concentration bounds over the Haar-random test-noise eigenbases apply to the fixed limiting direction.

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:main-coordinate-reversal}
Let \(\lambda\in[0,1]\). 
Suppose that Assumptions~\ref{ass:aniso-clean}, \ref{ass:adam-init}, \ref{ass:lr-base}, and~\ref{ass:lr-momentum} hold with \(\Gamma=\Gamma_d\) and \(\Sigma_1=\cdots=\Sigma_k=\Sigma_{\lambda,d}\) as in \eqref{eq:coordinate-aligned-covariances}.
Suppose also that \(\log(1/\pi_{\min,d})=o(d)\), \(0<\inf_{a,d}\gamma_{a,d}\le\sup_{a,d}\gamma_{a,d}<\infty\), and the limits \(\bar\gamma_q:=\lim_{d\to\infty}d^{-1}\sum_{a=1}^d\gamma_{a,d}^q\) exist \(\forall q\in\{1/2,2\}\) and satisfy \(2\bar\gamma_{1/2}^2\bar\gamma_2>\pi\).\footnote{This requires a sufficiently dispersed spectrum. Corollary~\ref{cor:app-coordinate-dispersed-profiles} gives a sufficient condition.}
Then \(\lambda_c:=(\pi/(2\bar\gamma_{1/2}^2)-1)/(\bar\gamma_2-1)\) lies in \((0,1)\), and the following hold.\footnote{The same conclusions hold with RowGDM replaced by RowGD.}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2em,nosep]
    \item \emph{Diagonal covariance.} For every \(\lambda\in[0,1]\setminus\{\lambda_c\}\), there exist \(c_\lambda,C_\lambda>0\) such that, for every sufficiently large \(d\), with probability at least \(1-C_\lambda e^{-c_\lambda d}\) over the class means, for all \(\beta \in (0,1)\),
    \[
        \begin{aligned}
        \liminf_{t\to\infty}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{RowGDM}}\right)
        &>
        \limsup_{t\to\infty}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{Adam}}\right)
        &&\text{if }\lambda<\lambda_c,\\
        \liminf_{t\to\infty}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{Adam}}\right)
        &>
        \limsup_{t\to\infty}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{RowGDM}}\right)
        &&\text{if }\lambda>\lambda_c.
        \end{aligned}
    \]
    \item \emph{Recovery under Haar rotation.} Let \(Q\) be Haar-uniformly random on \(\mathsf{SO}(d)\) and independent of the class means, and replace every training and test input \(x\) by \(Qx\). There exist \(c_{\mathrm{rot}},C_{\mathrm{rot}}>0\) such that, for every fixed \(\lambda\in[0,1]\) and every sufficiently large \(d\), with probability at least \(1-C_{\mathrm{rot}}e^{-c_{\mathrm{rot}}d}\) over the class means and \(Q\), the RowGDM-over-Adam ordering holds.
\end{enumerate}

label: lem:app-general-lr-remainders
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Cumulative remainders for general learning rates

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix \(\varepsilon>0\) and choose \(T\) so that \(\eta_s^{q-1}\le\varepsilon\) for all \(s\ge T\). Then
\[
\frac{\sum_{s=0}^{t-1}\eta_s^q}{S_t}\le\frac{\sum_{s=0}^{T-1}\eta_s^q}{S_t}+\varepsilon,
\]
which proves the first limit. For the second assertion, enlarge \(T\ge t_0\) so that \(c\eta_s\le1\) for \(s\ge T\), and set \(A_s:=\sum_{\tau=t_0}^{s-1}\eta_\tau\). Since \(1-e^{-x}\ge x/2\) for \(x\in[0,1]\),
\[
e^{-cA_s}-e^{-cA_{s+1}}\ge\frac c2\eta_s e^{-cA_s}.
\]
The tail therefore telescopes to a bounded quantity, while the finite prefix is harmless.

label: lem:app-general-lr-normalization
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Normalization of a cumulative margin bound

title: Proof
body_md:
Since \(r_t=o(S_t)\) and \(S_t\to\infty\), the lower bound \(\Gamma S_t-r_t\) is positive for all sufficiently large \(t\). In particular, \(W_t\ne0\) eventually. For such \(t\),
\[
\frac{\mathfrak m(W_t)}{\psi(W_t)}\ge\frac{\Gamma S_t-r_t}{C_0+S_t}\longrightarrow\Gamma.
\]
This proves the liminf statement without imposing a sign condition on \(r_t\). When \(\Gamma=\Gamma_*\), positive homogeneity gives \(\mathfrak m(W_t)/\psi(W_t)\le\Gamma_*\), proving convergence. Compactness of the \(\psi\)-unit sphere and continuity of \(\mathfrak m\) give the accumulation-point statement.

label: lem:app-ms-basic
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Consequences of max--sum domination

title: Proof
body_md:
Since the \(\psi\)-unit ball is contained in the entrywise max-norm unit ball,
\[
\psi^*(G)=\max_{\psi(A)\le1}\langle G,A\rangle\le\max_{\|A\|_{\max}\le1}\langle G,A\rangle=\|G\|_{\mathrm{sum}}.
\]
Also, \(\|Ah\|_\infty\le\|A\|_{\max}\|h\|_1\le R_1(X)\psi(A)\). For \(v=Ah\), the softmax covariance bound gives \(v^\top H(s)v\le4(1-s_c)\|v\|_\infty^2\), which proves~\eqref{eq:app-ms-hessian}.

title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Full-batch max--sum dominated margin convergence

title: Proof
body_md:
The geometry-dependent steps in the normalized steepest-descent and momentum proofs of \citet[Appendices~D and E]{fan2026implicit} use only norm duality, the lower bound \(\psi^*(\nabla L(W))\ge\gamma_\psi(X)\mathcal G(W)\), the upper bound \(\psi^*(\nabla L(W))\le2R_1(X)\mathcal G(W)\), and the logit and Hessian controls in Lemma~\ref{lem:app-ms-basic}. Substituting these bounds into their pre-rate scalar argument gives
\[
\operatorname{mar}_X(W_t)\ge\gamma_\psi(X)S_t-r_t,\qquad \psi(W_t)\le\psi(W_0)+S_t,
\]
where \(r_t\) is a finite-prefix term plus sums of the forms \(\sum_s\eta_s^2\) and \(\sum_s\eta_s\exp(-c\sum_{\tau<s}\eta_\tau)\); in the momentum case, Assumption~\ref{ass:lr-momentum} controls the additional geometric-memory term. Lemma~\ref{lem:app-general-lr-remainders} gives \(r_t=o(S_t)\), and Lemma~\ref{lem:app-general-lr-normalization} with \(\mathfrak m=\operatorname{mar}_X\) and \(\Gamma=\Gamma_*=\gamma_\psi(X)\) proves the result.

label: lem:app-ga-atomic-package
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Geometry-adapted cross-entropy bounds

title: Proof
body_md:
For every \(c\in[k]\), norm duality gives
\[
|e_c^\top Ax_n|=|\langle A,e_cx_n^\top\rangle|\le\psi(A)\psi^*(e_cx_n^\top)\le R_\psi(X)\psi(A),
\]
which proves the first bound in~\eqref{eq:app-ga-logit-atom}; the second follows from the triangle inequality. Writing \(p_n(W):={\mathbb{S}}(Wx_n)\), the sample gradient has the decomposition
\[
\nabla\ell_n(W)=\sum_{c\ne y_n}p_{n,c}(W)(e_c-e_{y_n})x_n^\top,
\]
so
\[
\psi^*(\nabla\ell_n(W))\le2R_\psi(X)\bigl(1-p_{n,y_n}(W)\bigr).
\]
Averaging proves the upper bound in~\eqref{eq:app-ga-gradient-proxy}. For the lower bound, choose \(A_\star\) with \(\psi(A_\star)\le1\) and margin \(\gamma_\psi(X)\); then
\[
-\nabla L(W)=\frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N\sum_{c\ne y_n}p_{n,c}(W)(e_{y_n}-e_c)x_n^\top
\]
gives \(\psi^*(\nabla L(W))\ge\langle A_\star,-\nabla L(W)\rangle\ge\gamma_\psi(X)\mathcal G(W)\). For the Hessian bound, set \(v:=Ax_n\) and let \(C\) be categorical with law \(p_n(W)\). Then
\[
D^2\ell_n(W)[A,A]=\operatorname{Var}(v_C)\le\mathbb E[(v_C-v_{y_n})^2]\le4(1-p_{n,y_n}(W))\|v\|_\infty^2,
\]
which proves~\eqref{eq:app-ga-hessian}. Finally, convexity and the upper gradient bound, together with \(\mathcal G\le1\), yield \(L(U)-L(W)\le2R_\psi(X)\psi(U-W)\); exchanging \(U,W\) proves~\eqref{eq:app-ga-loss-lipschitz}.

label: lem:app-ga-stability-package
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Geometry-adapted softmax and gradient stability

title: Proof
body_md:
Set \(\delta_n:=(U-W)x_n\). Lemma~\ref{lem:app-ga-atomic-package} gives \(\|\delta_n\|_\infty\le h\), and the softmax formula gives
\[
\frac{p_{n,c}(U)}{p_{n,c}(W)}=e^{\delta_{n,c}}\frac{\sum_{a=1}^ke^{e_a^\top Wx_n}}{\sum_{a=1}^ke^{e_a^\top Wx_n+\delta_{n,a}}}\in[e^{-2h},e^{2h}].
\]
Summing over \(c\ne y_n\) proves the second ratio and~\eqref{eq:app-ga-proxy-stability}. If \(p:=p_n(W)\) and \(q:=p_n(U)\), the ratio bounds imply
\[
\sum_{c\ne y_n}|q_c-p_c|\le(e^{2h}-1)(1-p_{y_n}),\qquad |q_{y_n}-p_{y_n}|\le(e^{2h}-1)(1-p_{y_n}).
\]
Since \(\nabla\ell_n(U)-\nabla\ell_n(W)=(q-p)x_n^\top\),
\[
\psi^*((q-p)x_n^\top)\le\sum_{c=1}^k|q_c-p_c|\psi^*(e_cx_n^\top)\le2R_\psi(X)(e^{2h}-1)(1-p_{y_n}).
\]
Averaging over all samples proves~\eqref{eq:app-ga-full-gradient-stability}; averaging over \(B\), enlarging the resulting nonnegative sample sum to \([N]\), and using \(N/b=m\) proves~\eqref{eq:app-ga-batch-gradient-stability}.

label: lem:app-ga-batch-noise
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Random-reshuffling noise and cancellation

title: Proof
body_md:
When \(m\ge2\), let \(B^c=[N]\setminus B\). The finite-population identity
\[
\Xi_B(W)=\frac{m-1}{m}\bigl(\nabla L_B(W)-\nabla L_{B^c}(W)\bigr)
\]
and the single-sample bound in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:app-ga-atomic-package} give
\[
\psi^*(\Xi_B(W))\le\frac{m-1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N\psi^*(\nabla\ell_n(W))\le2(m-1)R_\psi(X)\mathcal G(W),
\]
while \(m=1\) is immediate.

For the second assertion, write \(\Xi_t(W):=\nabla L_{B_t}(W)-\nabla L(W)\). Every complete epoch satisfies \(\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}\Xi_{qm+r}(W)={\mathbf 0}\). Put \(K_\Xi(W):=2(m-1)R_\psi(X)\mathcal G(W)\). For a complete epoch contained in \(\{0,\ldots,t\}\), subtracting the constant coefficient \(\beta^{t-qm}\) and using \(1-\beta^r\le r(1-\beta)\) gives
\[
\psi^*\left(\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}\beta^{t-qm-r}\Xi_{qm+r}(W)\right)\le K_\Xi(W)\beta^{t-(q+1)m}(1-\beta)\frac{m(m-1)}2.
\]
Summing over complete epochs and using \((1-\beta)/(1-\beta^m)\le1\), then adding the at most \(m\) terms in the current incomplete epoch, gives
\[
\psi^*(E_t(W))\le(1-\beta)\frac{m(m+1)}2K_\Xi(W)=(1-\beta)m(m^2-1)R_\psi(X)\mathcal G(W).
\]

label: prop:app-ga-momentum-approximation
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Geometry-adapted random-reshuffling momentum control

label: eq:app-ga-momentum-decomposition
title: Proof
body_md:
Unrolling the momentum recursion and adding and subtracting frozen batch gradients at \(W_t\) gives
\begin{align}
M_{t+1}-\nabla L(W_t)=&(1-\beta)\sum_{\tau=0}^t\beta^\tau\Bigl(\nabla L_{B_{t-\tau}}(W_{t-\tau})-\nabla L_{B_{t-\tau}}(W_t)\Bigr)\nonumber\\
&+(1-\beta)\sum_{\tau=0}^t\beta^\tau\Bigl(\nabla L_{B_{t-\tau}}(W_t)-\nabla L(W_t)\Bigr)-\beta^{t+1}\nabla L(W_t).
\label{eq:app-ga-momentum-decomposition}
\end{align}
Lemma~\ref{lem:app-ga-stability-package} and~\eqref{eq:app-ga-path-length} bound the first term by
\[
2m(1-\beta)R_\psi(X)\mathcal G(W_t)\sum_{\tau=0}^t\beta^\tau\left(\exp\left(2R_\psi(X)\sum_{q=1}^{\tau}\eta_{t-q}\right)-1\right).
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:lr-momentum}, applied with \(c_1=2R_\psi(X)\), bounds the final sum by \(c_{\psi,\beta}\eta_t\) for all sufficiently large \(t\). Lemma~\ref{lem:app-ga-frozen-rr} controls the second term, and the upper gradient bound in~\eqref{eq:app-ga-gradient-proxy} controls the last, proving~\eqref{eq:app-ga-momentum-approximation}.

For the descent recurrence, the steepest-descent property and norm duality give
\begin{equation}
\langle\nabla L(W_t),\Delta_t\rangle\ge\psi^*(\nabla L(W_t))-2\psi^*(M_{t+1}-\nabla L(W_t)).
\label{eq:app-ga-first-order-alignment}
\end{equation}
The mean-value Taylor formula,~\eqref{eq:app-ga-hessian}, and \(\psi(\Delta_t)\le1\) bound the quadratic remainder in \(L(W_t-\eta_t\Delta_t)\) by
\[
2\eta_t^2R_\psi(X)^2\sup_{0\le s\le1}\mathcal G(W_t-s\eta_t\Delta_t).
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:app-ga-stability-package} bounds the supremum by \(e^{2R_\psi(X)\eta_0}\mathcal G(W_t)\). label: eq:app-det-gaussian-shell
title: Proof
body_md:
Put \(L_d:=\log(2N(d)(d+1))\) and \(a_d:=(L_d/d)^{1/4}\).
The assumptions \(\log N=o(d)\) and \(n_{\min}\to\infty\) imply \(a_d\to0\).
All normalized Gaussian vectors below obey the shell bound
\begin{equation}
\mathbb P\!\left(\left|\frac{\|g\|_2}{\sqrt d}-1\right|>t\right)\le2e^{-cdt^2},\qquad 0<t<1,
\label{eq:app-det-gaussian-shell}
\end{equation}
and every centered Gaussian scalar with variance at most \(C/d\) obeys \(\mathbb P(|Z|>t)\le2e^{-cdt^2/C}\).

Since \(\bar z_i\overset{\mathrm d}=g_i/\sqrt{n_i d}\), the event \(\max_i\|\bar z_i\|_2\le2/\sqrt{n_{\min}}\) fails with probability at most \(2N e^{-cd}\).
Thus
\begin{equation}
\max_i\|m_i-\mu_i\|_2\le\frac{2r_0}{\sqrt{n_{\min}}}=o(1)
\label{eq:app-det-mean-concentration}
\end{equation}
on an event whose failure probability is smaller than the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:app-det-common-event-probability}.
Applying \eqref{eq:app-det-gaussian-shell} to \(\mu_i\sim\mathcal N({\mathbf 0},I_d/d)\), with threshold \(Ca_d\), and taking a union bound proves \(\max_i|\|\mu_i\|_2-1|\le Ca_d\).
Conditionally on \(\mu_i\), the variable \(\mu_i^\top\mu_j\) is centered Gaussian with variance \(\|\mu_i\|_2^2/d\).
Another union bound over at most \(N^2\) ordered pairs gives \(\max_{i\ne j}|\mu_i^\top\mu_j|\le Ca_d\).
Combining these estimates with \eqref{eq:app-det-mean-concentration} proves (H1) and (H2).

Conditionally on all empirical means, \(m_j^\top e_{i,s}\) is centered Gaussian with variance at most \(r_0^2\|m_j\|_2^2/d\).
On the event \(\max_j\|m_j\|_2\le2\), a union bound over at most \(N^2\) triples gives \(\max_{i,j,s}|m_j^\top e_{i,s}|\le Ca_d\) with the required failure probability.
This proves (H3).
Items (H1)--(H2) imply \(\inf_{i\ne j}\|m_i-m_j\|_2\ge1\) and \(\inf_{i\ne j}\|\mu_i-\mu_j\|_2\ge1\) for all sufficiently large \(d\).
The normalization map is Lipschitz on vectors with norm at least one, so (H1) gives (H4).

For (H5), let \(s_i:=\operatorname{sign}(m_i)\in\{-1,1\}^d\).
Because each \(m_i\) is isotropic Gaussian, \(s_i\) is a uniform sign vector, and it is independent of every residual in its own class.
Bernstein's inequality for \(\|m_i\|_1\), Gaussian tails for \(s_j^\top m_i\) when \(i\ne j\), conditional Gaussian tails for \(s_j^\top e_{i,s}\), and a union bound give
\begin{equation}
\min_i\|m_i\|_1\ge\left(\sqrt{\frac2\pi}-o(1)\right)\sqrt d,\qquad \max_{i\ne j}|s_j^\top m_i|+\max_{i,j,s}|s_j^\top e_{i,s}|=o(\sqrt d)
\label{eq:app-det-sign-inputs}
\end{equation}
outside an event bounded as in \eqref{eq:app-det-common-event-probability}.
The matrix with rows \(w_i=t_ds_i\), where \(t_d\) is the reciprocal of the minimum bracket in
\begin{equation}
(s_i-s_j)^\top x_{i,s}\ge\|m_i\|_1-|s_j^\top m_i|-2\max_{\ell}|s_\ell^\top e_{i,s}|,
\label{eq:app-det-sign-margin}
\end{equation}
is feasible.
Equation \eqref{eq:app-det-sign-inputs} gives \(t_d\le(\sqrt{\pi/2}+o(1))/\sqrt d\), which is exactly (H5).

For (H6), each difference \(m_i-m_j\) is a centered isotropic Gaussian vector, even when \(n_i\ne n_j\), so \(u_{ij}^m\) is exactly uniform on \(\mathbb S^{d-1}\).
For one uniform direction, the two coordinate empirical processes in \eqref{eq:app-det-HJ} concentrate about \(A_{\max}\) and \(B_{\max}\) at rate \(e^{-cd\eta^2}\) for any fixed \(\tau\).
On the event \(d^{-1}\sum_\ell d u_\ell^2=1\), both processes are uniformly Lipschitz in \(\tau\).
A mesh of \([0,1]\) with spacing \(a_d\), followed by a union bound over the mesh and at most \(N^2\) ordered pairs, yields \eqref{eq:app-det-HJ-uniform} with error \(Ca_d\) and failure probability bounded by \eqref{eq:app-det-common-event-probability}.
Taking \(\varepsilon_d\) to dominate \(Ca_d\), \(2r_0/\sqrt{n_{\min}}\), and the deterministic vanishing envelopes in \eqref{eq:app-det-sign-inputs} completes the proof.

title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Quantitative Gaussian hard-edge count at the square aspect ratio

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $n:=n_d$ and take $T=1/16$. Since $n/d\to1$, for all sufficiently large $d$ we have $n/d\ge9/10$. Let $B$ be a fixed $n\times n$ coordinate submatrix of $H_d$, obtained by retaining a fixed set of $n$ rows when $p\ge d$ and a fixed set of $n$ columns when $p<d$. If $p\ge d$, then $H_d^\top H_d=B^\top B+R^\top R\succeq B^\top B$ for the matrix $R$ of deleted rows, while if $p<d$, then $H_dH_d^\top=BB^\top+RR^\top\succeq BB^\top$ for the matrix $R$ of deleted columns. Hence, by monotonicity of eigenvalues under the positive-semidefinite order,
\[
\sigma_j(H_d)\ge\sigma_j(B),\qquad 1\le j\le n.
\]

Fix $t\in[1/n,T]$ and put $\ell:=\lceil3nt\rceil$. For all sufficiently large $n$, the choice $T=1/16$ ensures $\ell<n$. Let $F$ be the $n\times(n-\ell)$ matrix obtained by retaining a fixed set of $n-\ell$ columns of $B$. Apply \citet[Corollary~5.35]{vershynin2012nonasymptotic} to $F$ with row dimension $N=n$, column dimension $n-\ell$, and deviation parameter $s:=t\sqrt n/4$. Then, except with probability at most
\[
2e^{-s^2/2}=2e^{-nt^2/32},
\]
we have
\[
\sigma_{\min}(F)\ge\sqrt n-\sqrt{n-\ell}-s=\sqrt n-\sqrt{n-\ell}-\frac{t\sqrt n}{4}.
\]
Using
\[
\sqrt n-\sqrt{n-\ell}=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt n+\sqrt{n-\ell}}\ge\frac{\ell}{2\sqrt n}\ge\frac32t\sqrt n,
\]
we obtain
\[
\sigma_{\min}(F)\ge\frac54t\sqrt n>t\sqrt d,
\]
where the last inequality holds for all sufficiently large $d$ because $n/d\to1$.

Writing $B=[F\ \ R_F]$, we have $BB^\top=FF^\top+R_FR_F^\top\succeq FF^\top$. Therefore the largest $n-\ell$ eigenvalues of $BB^\top$ are at least the $n-\ell$ positive eigenvalues of $FF^\top$, and hence
\[
\sigma_j(B)>t\sqrt d,\qquad 1\le j\le n-\ell.
\]
Together with $\sigma_j(H_d)\ge\sigma_j(B)$, this gives
\[
\frac1n\#\{j:\sigma_j(A_d)\le t\}\le\frac{\ell}{n}\le3t+\frac1n\le4t.
\]

Now fix $u\in[2/n,T]$ and take the dyadic grid $t_j=2^{-j}T$ down to the first grid point lying in $[u/2,u]$. Every such grid point is at least $u/2\ge1/n$, and the number of grid points is at most $C(1+\log(T/u))$. Applying the preceding fixed-threshold estimate at every grid point and taking a union bound, the probability that any of these estimates fails is at most
\[
C\bigl(1+\log(T/u)\bigr)e^{-cdu^2},
\]
because the smallest grid point is at least $u/2$ and $n/d\to1$. On the complementary event, for every $t\in[u,T]$ choose a dyadic grid point $t_j\in[t,2t]$; monotonicity of the counting function gives
\[
\frac1n\#\{\ell:\sigma_\ell(A_d)\le t\}\le\frac1n\#\{\ell:\sigma_\ell(A_d)\le t_j\}\le4t_j\le8t.
\]
Finally, $A_d$ has rank $n$ almost surely because the rank-deficient matrices form a Lebesgue-null algebraic set.

name: Positive margin growth and a trajectory-level coordinate bound

label: eq:app-adamproxy-trajectory-step-bound
title: Proof
body_md:
For finite \(W\), define
\[
\mathcal G(W):=\frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N(1-p_{n,y_n}(W)),\qquad R(W):=\sum_{(n,c)\in\mathcal Q}p_{n,c}(W)=N\mathcal G(W)>0,
\]
and let \(\theta_{n,c}(W):=p_{n,c}(W)/R(W)\).
Then \(\theta(W)\) belongs to the probability simplex \(\Delta(\mathcal Q)\).
For any \(\theta\in\Delta(\mathcal Q)\), write
\begin{align*}
Z_n(\theta)&:=\sum_{c\ne y_n}\theta_{n,c}A_{n,c},\qquad \mathsf S(\theta):=\sum_{n=1}^NZ_n(\theta),\\
\mathsf D_\kappa(\theta)&:=\left(\mathsf S(\theta)^{\odot2}+\kappa\sum_{n=1}^NZ_n(\theta)^{\odot2}\right)^{\odot1/2}.
\end{align*}
Since \(h_n(W)=R(W)Z_n(\theta(W))\), the common factor \(R(W)\) cancels in the proxy ratio, giving
\begin{equation}
\Psi_\kappa(W)=\mathsf S(\theta(W))\oslash\mathsf D_\kappa(\theta(W)),\qquad \|\Psi_\kappa(W)\|_{\max}\le1.
\label{eq:app-adamproxy-trajectory-step-bound}
\end{equation}
The coordinate bound follows from \(\mathsf D_\kappa(\theta)[\rho]\ge|\mathsf S(\theta)[\rho]|\), including zero denominators under the stated convention.
The entrywise inequalities \(|\mathsf S(\theta)|\le\sum_n|Z_n(\theta)|\) and \((\sum_nZ_n(\theta)^{\odot2})^{\odot1/2}\le\sum_n|Z_n(\theta)|\) imply
\begin{equation}
\|\mathsf D_\kappa(\theta)\|_{\mathrm{sum}}\le(1+\sqrt\kappa)\sum_n\|Z_n(\theta)\|_{\mathrm{sum}}\le2(1+\sqrt\kappa)R_1(X)=K_\kappa(X).
\label{eq:app-adamproxy-trajectory-metric-mass}
\end{equation}
Here the last inequality uses \(\|A_{n,c}\|_{\mathrm{sum}}=2\|x_n\|_1\) and \(\sum_{(n,c)\in\mathcal Q}\theta_{n,c}=1\).
Let \(V_*\) attain \(\gamma_{\max}(X)\) on the compact max-norm unit ball.
Max--sum duality and the margin constraints for \(V_*\) give
\[
\|\mathsf S(\theta)\|_{\mathrm{sum}}\ge\langle V_*,\mathsf S(\theta)\rangle=\sum_{(n,c)\in\mathcal Q}\theta_{n,c}\langle V_*,A_{n,c}\rangle\ge\gamma_{\max}(X).
\]
If \(\mathsf D_\kappa(\theta)[\rho]=0\), then \(\mathsf S(\theta)[\rho]=0\).
Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz on the remaining coordinates therefore yields
\begin{equation}
\mathcal J_\kappa(\theta):=\sum_{\rho:\mathsf D_\kappa(\theta)[\rho]>0}\frac{\mathsf S(\theta)[\rho]^2}{\mathsf D_\kappa(\theta)[\rho]}\ge\frac{\|\mathsf S(\theta)\|_{\mathrm{sum}}^2}{\|\mathsf D_\kappa(\theta)\|_{\mathrm{sum}}}\ge\rho_\kappa(X).
\label{eq:app-adamproxy-uniform-dissipation}
\end{equation}
Since \(\nabla L(W)=-\mathcal G(W)\mathsf S(\theta(W))\), it follows that
\begin{equation}
-\langle\nabla L(W),\Psi_\kappa(W)\rangle=\mathcal G(W)\mathcal J_\kappa(\theta(W))\ge\rho_\kappa(X)\mathcal G(W).
\label{eq:app-adamproxy-uniform-descent}
\end{equation}

To control the discrete-time remainder, fix \(\|\Delta\|_{\max}\le1\).
Then \(\|\Delta x_n\|_\infty\le R_1(X)\), and the softmax Hessian satisfies
\[
D^2\ell_n(V)[\Delta,\Delta]=\operatorname{Var}_{C\sim p_n(V)}\bigl((\Delta x_n)_C\bigr)\le4R_1(X)^2\bigl(1-p_{n,y_n}(V)\bigr).
\]
Indeed, the variance is at most the second moment about \((\Delta x_n)_{y_n}\), and every logit difference has magnitude at most \(2R_1(X)\).
The softmax formula also gives \(\mathcal G(W+sa\Delta)\le e^{2R_1(X)a}\mathcal G(W)\) for \(a\ge0\) and \(s\in[0,1]\).
Because \(a_t\to0\), the quantity \(a_{\max}:=\sup_ta_t\) is finite.
Taylor's formula, \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-trajectory-step-bound}, and \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-uniform-descent} consequently imply
\begin{equation}
L(W_{t+1})\le L(W_t)-a_t\bigl(\rho_\kappa(X)-C_Xa_t\bigr)\mathcal G(W_t),\qquad C_X:=2R_1(X)^2e^{2R_1(X)a_{\max}}.
\label{eq:app-adamproxy-trajectory-loss-descent}
\end{equation}
For all sufficiently large \(t\), the coefficient in parentheses is at least \(\rho_\kappa(X)/2\), so \(L(W_t)\) is eventually nonincreasing and has a nonnegative limit.
If this limit were \(L_\infty>0\), then at each sufficiently large \(t\) some sample would satisfy \(\ell_n(W_t)\ge L(W_t)\ge L_\infty\), and hence \(\mathcal G(W_t)\ge(1-e^{-L_\infty})/N>0\).
Summing \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-trajectory-loss-descent} would contradict \(L\ge0\) and \(\sum_ta_t=\infty\).
Thus \(L(W_t)\to0\).
Since \(0\le\ell_n(W_t)\le NL(W_t)\), every sample loss tends to zero, and
\[
\frac{\mathcal G(W_t)}{L(W_t)}=\frac{\sum_n(1-e^{-\ell_n(W_t)})}{\sum_n\ell_n(W_t)}\longrightarrow1.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\ell_n(W)=\log\left(1+\sum_{c\ne y_n}e^{-\langle W,A_{n,c}\rangle}\right)
\]
shows that every training margin tends to infinity.
For all sufficiently large \(t\), dividing \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-trajectory-loss-descent} by \(L(W_t)\) and applying \(-\log(1-z)\ge z\) gives
\[
-\log L(W_{t+1})+\log L(W_t)\ge a_t\bigl(\rho_\kappa(X)-C_Xa_t\bigr)\frac{\mathcal G(W_t)}{L(W_t)}.
\]
The factor multiplying \(a_t\) converges to \(\rho_\kappa(X)\), so summation and weighted Ces\`aro averaging yield
\[
\liminf_{t\to\infty}\frac{-\log L(W_t)}{T_t}\ge\rho_\kappa(X).
\]
Write \(m_t:=\operatorname{mar}_X(W_t)\).
Once \(m_t\ge0\), a sample attaining the minimum margin gives
\[
L(W_t)\ge\frac1N\log(1+e^{-m_t})\ge\frac{e^{-m_t}}{2N},\qquad m_t\ge-\log L(W_t)-\log(2N).
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-linear-margin-growth}.
Finally, \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-trajectory-step-bound} gives \(\|W_t\|_{\max}\le\|W_0\|_{\max}+T_t\).
Combining this bound with \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-linear-margin-growth} proves \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-positive-normalized-margin} and \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-coordinate-cap}.

body_md:
\label{lem:app-adamproxy-clipped-barrier}
Let \(u_{d,\xi}\in\mathbb S^{d-1}\) be indexed by a nonempty finite set \(\mathcal I_d\), and suppose the empirical functions in \eqref{eq:app-det-HJ} satisfy
\[
\sup_{\xi\in\mathcal I_d}\sup_{\tau\in[0,1]}\left(\left|H_{u_{d,\xi}}(\tau)-A_{\max}(\tau)\right|+\left|J_{u_{d,\xi}}(\tau)-B_{\max}(\tau)\right|\right)\longrightarrow0.
\]
Fix \(a\ge3\), let \(a_d\to a\) and \(\upsilon_d\to\sqrt2\) be positive deterministic sequences, and define
\[
\mathcal V_{d,\xi}:=\left\{v\in\mathbb R^d:\|v\|_\infty\le\frac{a_d}{\sqrt d},\quad v^\top u_{d,\xi}\ge\upsilon_d\right\}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(d\), these sets are nonempty and
\begin{equation}
\inf_{\xi\in\mathcal I_d}\inf_{v\in\mathcal V_{d,\xi}}\left\|\frac{v}{\|v\|_2}-u_{d,\xi}\right\|_2\ge\delta_{\mathrm{clip}}(a)-o_d(1).
\label{eq:app-adamproxy-clipped-conclusion}
\end{equation}
The error depends only on the uniform empirical errors and the deviations of \(a_d\) and \(\upsilon_d\) from their limits.

name: Uniform clipped-Gaussian angular barrier

title: Proof
body_md:
Since \(\upsilon_d/a_d\to\sqrt2/a<A_{\max}(1)\), uniform convergence gives \(0<\upsilon_d/a_d<H_{u_{d,\xi}}(1)\) for every \(\xi\) and all sufficiently large \(d\).
The feasibility condition in Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-clipped-exact} therefore holds, and that proposition gives
\[
\mathfrak m_{d,\xi}:=\min_{v\in\mathcal V_{d,\xi}}\|v\|_2=a_d\sqrt{J_{u_{d,\xi}}(\widehat\tau_{d,\xi})},\qquad H_{u_{d,\xi}}(\widehat\tau_{d,\xi})=\frac{\upsilon_d}{a_d},
\]
with \(\widehat\tau_{d,\xi}\in(0,1)\).
Uniform convergence and strict monotonicity of \(A_{\max}\) imply
\[
\sup_{\xi\in\mathcal I_d}|\widehat\tau_{d,\xi}-\tau_a|\longrightarrow0,\qquad \sup_{\xi\in\mathcal I_d}\left|\mathfrak m_{d,\xi}-a\sqrt{B_{\max}(\tau_a)}\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
For every \(v\in\mathcal V_{d,\xi}\), the vector \(y=(\upsilon_d/(v^\top u_{d,\xi}))v\) also belongs to \(\mathcal V_{d,\xi}\).
Hence
\[
\frac{v^\top u_{d,\xi}}{\|v\|_2}\le\frac{\upsilon_d}{\mathfrak m_{d,\xi}}=C_{\mathrm{clip}}(a)+o_d(1),
\]
where the error is independent of \(v\) and uniform over \(\xi\).
The identity \(\|v/\|v\|_2-u\|_2^2=2-2v^\top u/\|v\|_2\) proves \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-clipped-conclusion}.

title: Proof
body_md:
The event guarantees separability, and Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-common-event}(H5) and \eqref{eq:app-stoch-data-radius-bounds} give
\[
r_{\max}^*(X)\le\frac{\sqrt{2\pi}+o_d(1)}{2\sqrt d},\qquad \max_n\|x_n\|_2\le R_*,\qquad R_1(X)\le\sqrt d\,R_*.
\]
Applying Proposition~\ref{prop:app-adamproxy-coordinate-cap} and \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-kappa-bound}, we obtain
\begin{align*}
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\sqrt d\left\|\frac{W_t^{\mathrm{AP}}}{\operatorname{mar}_X(W_t^{\mathrm{AP}})}\right\|_{\max}&\le2(1+\sqrt{\overline\kappa})dR_*r_{\max}^*(X)^2\\
&\le C_{\mathrm{AP}}+o_d(1).
\end{align*}
For all sufficiently large \(d\), the right-hand side is less than \(C_{\mathrm{AP}}+1/4\).
The definition of the time limsup and the unit margin of the normalized iterates then give \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-eventual-capped-membership}.
In particular, \(\mathcal C_d\) is nonempty.

Fix \(V\in\mathcal C_d\) and an ordered pair \(i\ne j\), and write \(v:=v_i-v_j\) and \(u:=u_{ij}^m\).
The coordinate cap gives
\[
\|v\|_\infty\le\frac{2C_{\mathrm{AP}}+1}{\sqrt d}\le\frac{a_{\mathrm{AP}}}{\sqrt d}.
\]
Averaging feasibility over the samples from classes \(i\) and \(j\) gives \(v^\top m_i\ge1\) and \(v^\top m_j\le-1\), and hence
\[
v^\top u\ge\frac{2}{\|m_i-m_j\|_2}\ge\sqrt2-o_d(1).
\]
The last error is deterministic and uniform over all pairs and all \(V\in\mathcal C_d\), by Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-common-event}(H2).
Choose a positive deterministic sequence \(\upsilon_d\to\sqrt2\) below these projection lower bounds.
Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-common-event}(H6) supplies the empirical estimates in Lemma~\ref{lem:app-adamproxy-clipped-barrier}, which applies with \(a_d=a_{\mathrm{AP}}\) and \(\mathcal I_d=\{(i,j):i\ne j\}\).
Thus \(\|u_{ij}^V-u_{ij}^m\|_2\ge\delta_{\mathrm{AP}}-o_d(1)\) uniformly over all pairs and all \(V\in\mathcal C_d\).
Finally, Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-common-event}(H4) and the reverse triangle inequality prove \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-boundary-separation}.

label: eq:app-adamproxy-set-error-order
title: Proof
body_md:
Set \(\beta_1:=\beta_{\mathrm{AP}}\), fix \(\beta\in[\beta_1,1)\), and let \(\mathcal R_d\) be the Gaussian radial event from Lemma~\ref{lem:app-acc-gaussian-radial-event}.
Define \(\mathcal H_d:=\mathcal E_d^{\mathrm{near}}\cap\mathcal R_d\).
By \eqref{eq:app-stoch-near-event-probability} and \eqref{eq:app-acc-radial-event-probability}, for every sufficiently large \(d\),
\[
\mathbb P(\mathcal H_d)\ge1-e^{-\sqrt d}.
\]
Work on \(\mathcal H_d\), and take
\[
\mathcal R_d^{\mathrm{clf}}:=\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row},\beta,b_d}^X,\qquad \mathcal C_d^{\mathrm{clf}}:=\mathcal C_d.
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:app-adamproxy-row-control} and Proposition~\ref{prop:app-adamproxy-boundary-separation} give, for all sufficiently large \(d\),
\[
\sup_{U\in\mathcal R_d^{\mathrm{clf}}}\max_{i\ne j}\|u_{ij}^U-u_{ij}^{\mu}\|_2\le h_{\mathrm{AP}},\qquad \inf_{V\in\mathcal C_d}D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(V)\ge\frac{\delta_{\mathrm{AP}}}{2}.
\]
The radial deviations tend to zero on \(\mathcal R_d\) under a deterministic envelope, and the limiting amplitude condition is \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-amplitude-gap}.
Choose fixed constants \(0<b_*<a_*\) with \(\mathsf b(\delta_{\mathrm{AP}}/2)<b_*<a_*<\mathsf a(h_{\mathrm{AP}})\).
Proposition~\ref{prop:app-acc-finite-bounds} gives, for \(\sigma_d=r_{\mathrm{te}}/\sqrt d\) and all sufficiently large \(d\),
\begin{align*}
\sup_{U\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row},\beta,b_d}^X}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(U)&\le(k-1)\overline\Phi(a_*/\sigma_d),\\
\inf_{V\in\mathcal C_d}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(V)&\ge2\pi_{\min,d}\overline\Phi(b_*/\sigma_d).
\end{align*}
The Gaussian upper-tail inequality \(\overline\Phi(x)/\overline\Phi(y)\le e^{-(x^2-y^2)/2}\) for \(x\ge y\ge0\) therefore yields
\[
\frac{\sup_{U\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row},\beta,b_d}^X}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(U)}{\inf_{V\in\mathcal C_d}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(V)}\le\frac{k-1}{2\pi_{\min,d}}\exp\left(-\frac{(a_*^2-b_*^2)d}{2r_{\mathrm{te},0}^2}\right)\longrightarrow0,
\]
since \(k=O(d)\), \(\log(1/\pi_{\min,d})=o(d)\), and \(r_{\mathrm{te},0}:=\sup_dr_{\mathrm{te}}(d)<\infty\).
Consequently, for every sufficiently large \(d\) on \(\mathcal H_d\),
\begin{equation}
\sup_{U\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row},\beta,b_d}^X}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(U)<\inf_{V\in\mathcal C_d}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(V).
\label{eq:app-adamproxy-set-error-order}
\end{equation}
The positive Row effective margin and Corollary~\ref{cor:app-ga-margin-transfer} give
\[
d_{\cos}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{RR\text{-}RowSGDM}},\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row},\beta,b_d}^X\right)\longrightarrow0.
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:app-acc-trajectory-continuity} hence implies
\[
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{RR\text{-}RowSGDM}}\right)\le\sup_{U\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row},\beta,b_d}^X}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(U).
\]
For AdamProxy, \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-eventual-capped-membership} and positive scale invariance of population error give
\[
\liminf_{t\to\infty}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(W_t^{\mathrm{AP}})\ge\inf_{V\in\mathcal C_d}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(V).
\]
Combining these two bounds with \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-set-error-order} yields
\[
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{RR\text{-}RowSGDM}}\right)<\liminf_{t\to\infty}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(W_t^{\mathrm{AP}}).
\]
Since \(\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}=1-\mathcal E_{\pi,d}\), this is the claimed accuracy ordering.
The Row momentum estimates hold for every reshuffling realization, and the AdamProxy estimates are deterministic conditional on the training data, so no additional exceptional event is required.

title: Proof
body_md:
The factorization follows directly from \(h_n(W)=\sum_{c\ne y_n}p_{n,c}(W)A_{n,c}\). For every coordinate \(\rho\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives \(\mathsf S(\theta)[\rho]^2\le N\mathsf Q(\theta)[\rho]\), and therefore
\[
\mathsf D_{N,b}(\theta)[\rho]^2-\mathsf S(\theta)[\rho]^2=\frac{N-b}{b(N-1)}\left(N\mathsf Q(\theta)[\rho]-\mathsf S(\theta)[\rho]^2\right)\ge0.
\]
Hence \(\mathsf D_{N,b}(\theta)[\rho]\ge|\mathsf S(\theta)[\rho]|\), and if \(\mathsf D_{N,b}(\theta)[\rho]=0\), then \(\mathsf S(\theta)[\rho]=0\). With the convention \(0/0:=0\), this proves \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-coefficient-proxy} and the coordinate bound. By linear separability, choose \(V\) and \(\sigma_{\mathrm{sep}}>0\) with \(\langle V,A_q\rangle\ge\sigma_{\mathrm{sep}}\) for every \(q\). Since \(\mathsf D_{N,b}\) is continuous on the compact simplex, \(D_{\max}:=\max_\theta\|\mathsf D_{N,b}(\theta)\|_{\max}<\infty\), and
\[
\sigma_{\mathrm{sep}}\le\langle V,\mathsf S(\theta(W))\rangle\le\|V\|_{\mathrm F}D_{\max}\|\Psi_{N,b}(W)\|_{\mathrm F}.
\]
Thus \(\|\Psi_{N,b}(W_t)\|_{\mathrm F}\) is bounded above and below by positive constants. Since \(\Psi_{N,b}(W)=-\Phi_{N,b}(W)\), the normalized descent-proxy directions satisfy \(\Psi_{N,b}(W_t)/\|\Psi_{N,b}(W_t)\|_{\mathrm F}\to-\overline\Phi\). Assumption~\ref{ass:lr-base} implies that the epochwise schedule \(\gamma_t\) is positive, tends to zero, and satisfies \(\sum_t\gamma_t=\infty\). With \(T_t:=\sum_{s=0}^{t-1}\gamma_s\|\Psi_{N,b}(W_s)\|_{\mathrm F}\), one has \(T_t\to\infty\) and
\[
\frac{W_t}{T_t}=\frac{W_0}{T_t}+\frac1{T_t}\sum_{s=0}^{t-1}\gamma_s\|\Psi_{N,b}(W_s)\|_{\mathrm F}\frac{\Psi_{N,b}(W_s)}{\|\Psi_{N,b}(W_s)\|_{\mathrm F}}\longrightarrow-\overline\Phi.
\]
Hence \(\|W_t\|_{\mathrm F}/T_t\to1\) and \(W_t/\|W_t\|_{\mathrm F}\to-\overline\Phi\), proving \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-Wbar-sign}. Compactness of \(\Delta(\mathcal Q)\) and the two-sided bound on \(\|\Psi_{N,b}(W_t)\|_{\mathrm F}\) give a subsequence satisfying \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-selected-subsequence}. The separator inequality passes to the limit and gives \(\mathsf S(\theta^\star)\ne{\mathbf 0}\), while \(\|\Psi_{N,b}(W_{t_j})\|_{\max}\le1\) yields \(\nu\|\overline W\|_{\max}\le1\).

title: Proof
body_md:
For a unit vector \(u\) independent of \(O_i\), write \(O_i^\top u=g/\|g\|_2\). The quadratic form is
\[
u^\top\Sigma_i u=\frac{d}{\|g\|_2^2T_{s_\Sigma,d}}\sum_{r=1}^d r^{-s_\Sigma}g_r^2.
\]
When \(s_\Sigma<1\), weighted chi-square concentration gives deviations \(o(1)\) with failure at most \(e^{-d^\chi}\) for every \(\chi<1-s_\Sigma\). A union bound over the finite number of selectors and their \(O(k^2)=O(d^2)\) pair directions proves \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-low-residual-energy}.

Now suppose \(s_\Sigma\ge1\). Laurent--Massart's inequality gives, for every \(t>0\),
\[
\frac1{T_{s_\Sigma,d}}\sum_{r=1}^dr^{-s_\Sigma}g_r^2\le1+\frac{2\sqrt{T_{2s_\Sigma,d}t}+2t}{T_{s_\Sigma,d}}
\]
except with probability \(e^{-t}\), while \(\|g\|_2^2/d=1+o(1)\) exponentially fast. Taking \(t=(2+b)\log d\) and union-bounding over \(O(d^2)\) selected Row pair directions gives \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-row-sharp-energy}; the square-root term is \(o(c_d)\).


For the competitor lower bound, fix \(q\in(0,1)\) and \(0<a<1-q\), and choose \(q_+\in(q,1-a)\). Write \(L_d:=\log d\), let \(h_i:=O_ie_1\), and represent \(h_i=\xi_i/\|\xi_i\|_2\) using independent \(\xi_i\sim\mathcal N({\mathbf 0},I_d)\). Fix one selected competitor and its code \((a_i^\psi)\) and edge set \(\mathcal G_d^\psi\) from Lemma~\ref{lem:app-aniso-clean-quantified-mean}. Put \(t_d:=\sqrt{2q_+L_d}\) and define
\[
N_d:=\sum_{(i,j)\in\mathcal G_d^\psi}\mathbf 1\{\xi_i^\top a_i^\psi\ge t_d,\ \xi_i^\top a_j^\psi\le-t_d\}.
\]
The coherence bound \(\max_{i\ne j}|(a_i^\psi)^\top a_j^\psi|=o(1/L_d)\) implies, uniformly over the relevant distinct indices,
\[
\mathbb P(\xi_i^\top a_i^\psi\ge t_d,\xi_i^\top a_j^\psi\le-t_d)=d^{-2q_++o(1)},\qquad \mathbb P(\xi_i^\top a_i^\psi\ge t_d,\xi_i^\top a_j^\psi\le-t_d,\xi_i^\top a_\ell^\psi\le-t_d)=d^{-3q_++o(1)}.
\]
Indeed, the two- and three-dimensional covariance matrices differ from the identity by \(o(1/L_d)\), and Gaussian density comparison on the relevant orthants changes the logarithmic tail asymptotics by \(o(L_d)\). Edge indicators with different first indices are independent. Since \(|\mathcal G_d^\psi|=\Theta(d^2)\),
\[
\mathbb E N_d=d^{2-2q_++o(1)},\qquad \operatorname{Var}(N_d)\le\mathbb E N_d+d^{3-3q_++o(1)}.
\]
Chebyshev's inequality gives
\begin{equation}
\mathbb P(N_d=0)\le d^{-(1-q_+)+o(1)}=o(d^{-a}).
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-extreme-failure}
\end{equation}
On \(\{N_d>0\}\), choose a counted edge using a fixed ordering of \(\mathcal G_d^\psi\). This choice depends only on the class-side information and \((\xi_i)_{i=1}^k\), not on the remaining residual eigenframes. Uniform Gaussian norm concentration and \(\|a_i^\psi-a_j^\psi\|_2=\sqrt2+o(1)\) give
\[
h_i^\top p_{ij}^\psi\ge\frac{2t_d}{(1+o(1))\sqrt{2d}}.
\]
For any fixed \(A>0\), spherical concentration and a union bound give, except with probability \(O(d^{-A})\),
\[
\max_{(i,j)\in\mathcal G_d^\psi}\sqrt d\,\left|h_i^\top(u_{ij}^{U_\psi}-p_{ij}^\psi)\right|\le C_A L_d^{-1/2},\qquad \max_{i\ne j}d\left|h_i^\top u_{ij}^{U_\psi}\right|^2\le C_A L_d.
\]
Here the first bound uses \(\|u_{ij}^{U_\psi}-p_{ij}^\psi\|_2\le L_d^{-1}\), and all directions in these bounds are fixed after conditioning on the class-side information. The selected edge therefore satisfies
\[
d\bigl(h_i^\top u_{ij}^{U_\psi}\bigr)^2\ge(4q_+-o(1))L_d\ge4qL_d
\]
for all sufficiently large \(d\). Since the top eigenvalue of \(\Sigma_i\) is \(d/T_{s_\Sigma,d}\), its contribution is at least \(4qc_d\).

Suppose \(s_\Sigma=1\). Conditional on all top eigenvectors, their auxiliary Gaussian radii, and the selected edge, the remaining eigenframe of \(O_i\) is Haar on \(h_i^\perp\). Write \(a_{ij}:=h_i^\top u_{ij}^{U_\psi}\). The remaining contribution has the conditional distribution
\[
\frac{d(1-a_{ij}^2)}{T_{1,d}}\frac{\sum_{r=2}^d r^{-1}g_r^2}{\sum_{r=2}^d g_r^2},\qquad g_2,\ldots,g_d\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
The preceding upper bound gives \(a_{ij}^2=O(L_d/d)\). The weighted chi-square lower-tail inequality, with tail parameter \(L_d^{3/2}\), gives
\[
\sum_{r=2}^d r^{-1}g_r^2\ge T_{1,d}-1-O(L_d^{3/4})
\]
except with probability \(\exp(-L_d^{3/2})\), since \(\sum_{r=2}^d r^{-2}=O(1)\). Also, \(\sum_{r=2}^d g_r^2=(d-1)(1+O(L_d^{-2}))\) except with probability \(C\exp(-cd/L_d^4)\). Thus the remaining contribution is at least \(1-O(L_d^{-1/4})=1-o(1)\) with superpolynomial confidence. Choosing \(A>a\), integrating these conditional bounds, and using \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-extreme-failure} proves \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-competitor-extreme-energy} with failure at most \(C_{q,a}d^{-a}\). A finite union handles all selected competitors.

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose first that \(s_\Sigma<1\). Fix \(0<\chi<\min\{1-s_\mu,1-s_\Sigma\}\), choose \(\chi_+\in(\chi,\min\{1-s_\mu,1-s_\Sigma\})\), and fix \(0<\varepsilon_0<1-\vartheta_\alpha\). Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:app-aniso-clean-quantified-mean} and Lemma~\ref{lem:app-aniso-clean-sharp-common}(i) with confidence exponent \(\chi_+\) implies that every selected Row direction has
\[
Z_{i\to j}(U_{\mathrm{row}})^2\ge(1/2-o(1))d
\]
uniformly over all directed pairs, whereas every selected competitor \(U_\psi\) has a directed pair with
\[
[Z_{i\to j}(U_\psi)]_+^2\le\frac{\vartheta_\psi+\varepsilon_0}{2}\,d+o(d).
\]
Since \(\vartheta_\psi+\varepsilon_0<1\), the competitor-to-Row squared-signal ratio has limsup strictly below one. The Row coefficient is of order \(d\), and \(\log((k-1)/\pi_{\min,d})=o(d/\log d)=o(d)\), so Lemma~\ref{lem:app-aniso-error-comparison} gives the strict accuracy ordering. The two mean and residual events have joint failure at most \(e^{-d^\chi}\) after increasing the dimension threshold.




Now suppose \(s_\Sigma\ge1\). Fix \(\zeta\) satisfying \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-zeta-range}, choose \(b>\zeta\) sufficiently close to \(\zeta\), and then choose \(q\) so that
\begin{equation}
\vartheta_\alpha\left(1+\frac b2\right)<q<1-\zeta.
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-bq-choice}
\end{equation}

title: Lemma

name: Deterministic whole-face stability

label: eq:when2-quant-averaged-constraint
title: Proof
body_md:
The matrix with rows \(\mu_i/(1-2\varepsilon)\) is feasible, so the optimal row radius \(R_*\) is at most \(\sqrt{1+\varepsilon}/(1-2\varepsilon)\le1+C\varepsilon\).
For any feasible \(W\), averaging the class-\(i\) constraints over competitors gives
\begin{equation}
(w_i-\bar w)^\top\mu_i\ge1-\frac1k,\qquad \bar w:=\frac1k\sum_iw_i.
\label{eq:when2-quant-averaged-constraint}
\end{equation}
For a Row minimizer, Cauchy--Schwarz and the row variance identity therefore imply
\[
\frac{(1-1/k)^2}{1+\varepsilon}\le\frac1k\sum_i\|w_i-\bar w\|_2^2\le R_*^2-\|\bar w\|_2^2.
\]
Thus \(\|\bar w\|_2\le C\varepsilon^{1/2}\), and \eqref{eq:when2-quant-averaged-constraint} gives \(w_i^\top\mu_i\ge1-C\varepsilon^{1/2}\) uniformly in \(i\).
Expanding \(\|w_i-\mu_i\|_2^2\) proves \eqref{eq:when2-quant-row-stability}.

The sign matrix divided by \(\sqrt d(h-2\varepsilon)\) is feasible, so \(t_{\max}\le[\sqrt d(h-2\varepsilon)]^{-1}\).
Fix a Max minimizer and set \(H=W/t_{\max}\), \(\bar H=k^{-1}\sum_iH_i\), and
\[
D_i:=\frac{\|\mu_i\|_1-H_i^\top\mu_i}{\sqrt d}\ge0.
\]
Since \(\|H\|_{\max}=1\), averaging \eqref{eq:when2-quant-averaged-constraint} over \(i\) yields
\begin{align*}
\frac1k\sum_iD_i&\le h+\varepsilon-\frac{1-1/k}{t_{\max}\sqrt d}-\frac{\bar H^\top\bar\mu}{\sqrt d}\\
&\le h+\varepsilon-(1-1/k)(h-2\varepsilon)+\|\bar\mu\|_2\le C\varepsilon.
\end{align*}
For every \(s>0\), the coordinate bound on \(H\) gives
\begin{equation}
\frac{\|H_i-T_i\|_2^2}{d}\le\frac{2D_i}{s}+\frac4d\#\{a:\sqrt d\,|\mu_i[a]|\le s\}.
\label{eq:when2-diet-threshold-split}
\end{equation}
Indeed, outside the indicated small-coordinate set, use \((H_i[a]-T_i[a])^2\le2(1-H_i[a]T_i[a])\), and use the bound four on that set.
Taking \(s=\varepsilon^{1/2}\) and averaging gives \(\|H-T\|_{\mathrm F}^2/(kd)\le C\varepsilon^{1/2}\).
Moreover, \(\|k^{-1}\sum_iT_i\|_2^2/d\le k^{-1}+\varepsilon\le2\varepsilon\), so Jensen's inequality gives \(\|\bar H\|_2/\sqrt d\le C\varepsilon^{1/4}\).
Returning to the individual constraints now yields
\[
D_i\le h+\varepsilon-(1-1/k)(h-2\varepsilon)+\frac{\|\bar H\|_2\|\mu_i\|_2}{\sqrt d}\le C\varepsilon^{1/4}.
\]
Taking \(s=\varepsilon^{1/8}\) in \eqref{eq:when2-diet-threshold-split} proves the claimed uniform row error for \(H\).
Finally, averaging the constraints and using \(H_i^\top\mu_i\le\|\mu_i\|_1\) gives
\[
h-2\varepsilon\le\frac1{t_{\max}\sqrt d}\le\frac{h+2\varepsilon}{1-1/k}=h+O(\varepsilon).
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:when2-quant-max-stability}.
The feasible witnesses and compact norm sublevel sets ensure existence of both minima.

label: lem:when2-diet-aligned-geometry
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Quantitative whole-face geometry in aligned coordinates

title: Proof
body_md:
We verify the inputs of Lemma~\ref{lem:when2-quant-deterministic-rigidity} at precision \(\varepsilon\).
The independent-coordinate Gaussian quadratic-form and Bernstein bounds used below follow, for example, from the concentration tools in \citet{vershynin2012nonasymptotic}.
For the quadratic terms, the identity \(\mathbb E e^{u(Z^2-1)}=e^{-u}(1-2u)^{-1/2}\) for \(|u|<1/2\), together with the bounded spectral weights, gives deviation probability at most \(2e^{-cd\varepsilon^2}\) for each normalized quadratic form.
Polarization gives the corresponding bilinear bounds.
The variables \(\sqrt{\gamma_{a,d}}|g_i[a]|\) have uniformly bounded exponential moments, so Bernstein's inequality gives
\[
\mathbb P\!\left(\left|\frac{\|\mu_i\|_1}{\sqrt d}-h_d\right|>\varepsilon\right)\le2e^{-cd\varepsilon^2}.
\]
For \(j\ne i\), conditioning on \(T_j\) gives \(T_j^\top\mu_i/\sqrt d\sim\mathcal N(0,1/d)\).
The products \(T_i[a]T_j[a]\) are independent Rademacher variables across \(a\), so their averages satisfy the same exponential bound.
For either prescribed threshold \(s\), Gaussian small-ball probabilities and Hoeffding's inequality give
\[
\mathbb P\!\left(\frac1d\#\{a:\sqrt d\,|\mu_i[a]|\le s\}>Ks+\varepsilon\right)\le e^{-2d\varepsilon^2},
\]
where \(K\) depends only on \(c_\Gamma\).
Also, \(\bar\mu\) has covariance \(\Gamma_d/(kd)\); when \(k\ge C\varepsilon^{-2}\), the event \(\|\bar\mu\|_2>\varepsilon\) has probability at most \(Ce^{-cd}\).
All coordinates are nonzero almost surely, and \(g_0\sqrt{c_\Gamma}\le h_d\le g_0<1\).
A union bound over these \(O(k^2)\) events verifies the deterministic lemma's hypotheses and proves \eqref{eq:when2-diet-row-rigidity}--\eqref{eq:when2-diet-aligned-laws}.

For \eqref{eq:when2-quant-aligned-energies}, it suffices to treat \(\lambda=0,1\), since the quadratic forms and their asserted centers are affine in \(\lambda\).
The Gaussian difference \(\mu_i-\mu_j\) has covariance \(2\Gamma_d/d\), giving mean quadratic form \(2d^{-1}\operatorname{tr}(\Gamma_d\Sigma_\lambda)=2A_d(\lambda)\).
The same quadratic-form bound applies at both endpoints.
For the sign contrasts, \((T_i[a]-T_j[a])^2\) are independent across coordinates, lie in \(\{0,4\}\), and have mean two.
Their bounded weighted sums therefore concentrate about \(2\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\lambda=2d\) with failure at most \(2e^{-cd\varepsilon^2}\) at each endpoint.
Adding these events proves \eqref{eq:when2-quant-aligned-probability} and \eqref{eq:when2-quant-aligned-energies}.

title: Proof
body_md:
The spectral bounds give \(c_\Gamma I_d\preceq\Sigma_\lambda\preceq C_\Gamma I_d\) for every \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), since trace normalization implies \(c_\Gamma\le1\le C_\Gamma\).
For Row, \eqref{eq:when2-diet-row-rigidity} allows us to replace \(w_i-w_j\) by \(\mu_i-\mu_j\) with Euclidean error \(C\varepsilon^{1/4}\).
The latter vector has directed signal \(1+O(\varepsilon)\) and test-noise quadratic form \(2A_d(\lambda)+O(\varepsilon)\), uniformly over pairs and \(\lambda\).
The denominators are bounded away from zero, proving the first estimate in \eqref{eq:when2-diet-transition-coefficients}.
For Max, scale invariance allows us to use the contrast \((H_i-H_j)/\sqrt d\), where \(H=W/t_{\max}\).
By \eqref{eq:when2-diet-max-rigidity}, this contrast differs from \((T_i-T_j)/\sqrt d\) by at most \(C\varepsilon^{1/16}\).
The canonical sign contrast has directed signal \(h_d+O(\varepsilon)\) and test-noise quadratic form \(2+O(\varepsilon)\), proving the second estimate.
These arguments also prove the same estimates for every individual \(L_{i\to j}\).

Since \(\bar\gamma_{1/2}\le1\), we have \(0<h<1\); the condition \(h^2\bar\gamma_2>1\) implies \(\bar\gamma_2>1\) and \(0<\lambda_c<1\).
Fix \(\lambda\ne\lambda_c\), and let
\[
\Delta_\lambda:=\left|\frac1{2[1+\lambda(\bar\gamma_2-1)]}-\frac{h^2}{2}\right|>0.
\]
Choose a fixed \(\varepsilon>0\) small enough that the sum of the two errors in \eqref{eq:when2-diet-transition-coefficients} is at most \(\Delta_\lambda/4\).
By \eqref{eq:when2-diet-profile-limits}, the finite-dimensional coefficient gap has the asserted sign and magnitude at least \(3\Delta_\lambda/4\) for all sufficiently large \(d\).
Thus the complete-face gap is at least \(\Delta_\lambda/2\) on \(\mathcal A_d(\varepsilon)\).
Lemma~\ref{lem:when2-diet-error-transfer} proves the corresponding strict accuracy ordering.
Finally, \(k=\Theta(d)\) allows the factor \(k^2\) in \eqref{eq:when2-quant-aligned-probability} to be absorbed into \(C_\lambda e^{-c_\lambda d}\).
No convergence rate for either spectral summary is required; their convergence affects only the sufficiently-large-d threshold.

label: lem:when2-quant-haar-sign
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Quantitative sign statistics under a Haar rotation

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix a pair and choose an orthonormal basis \(F\in\mathbb R^{d\times m}\) of its span, where \(m\le2\).
Write \(x_i=Fu_i\), \(x_j=Fu_j\), and let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{d\times m}\) have independent standard Gaussian entries.
Then
\[
\sqrt d\,RF\ \overset{\mathrm d}=\ Y:=ZB,\qquad B:=(Z^\top Z/d)^{-1/2}.
\]
Indeed, \(Y/\sqrt d\) has orthonormal columns and its distribution is invariant under every left orthogonal transformation.
The Gaussian quadratic-form bound gives
\[
\mathbb P\!\left(\|Z^\top Z/d-I_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}>\varepsilon^3\right)\le Ce^{-cd\varepsilon^6}.
\]
On the complementary event, \(\|B-I_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C\varepsilon^3\), and hence
\[
\frac1d\|(Y-Z)u\|_2^2\le C\varepsilon^6
\]
for either coefficient vector \(u\).
Set \(X=Zu\), \(\widetilde X=Yu\), and \(b=\varepsilon^2\).
Gaussian small-ball probabilities and Hoeffding's inequality imply \(d^{-1}\#\{a:|X_a|\le b\}\le C\varepsilon^2\), except with probability \(Ce^{-cd\varepsilon^4}\).
Consequently,
\[
\frac1d\#\{a:\operatorname{sign}(\widetilde X_a)\ne\operatorname{sign}(X_a)\}\le\frac1d\#\{a:|X_a|\le b\}+\frac{\|\widetilde X-X\|_2^2}{db^2}\le C\varepsilon^2.
\]
Thus the normalized Euclidean distance between the corresponding sign vectors is at most \(C\varepsilon\).
By Cauchy--Schwarz, replacing \(Y\) by \(Z\) changes the empirical averages involving one sign factor and one linear factor by at most \(C\varepsilon\), while the empirical correlations between the corresponding sign vectors change by at most \(C\varepsilon^2\).
For a standard Gaussian row \(z^\top\) of \(Z\), the corresponding expectations are
\[
\mathbb E[\operatorname{sign}(z^\top u)z^\top v]=g_0\frac{u^\top v}{\|u\|_2},\qquad \mathbb E[\operatorname{sign}(z^\top u)\operatorname{sign}(z^\top v)]=\frac2\pi\arcsin\!\left(\frac{u^\top v}{\|u\|_2\|v\|_2}\right).
\]
The first identity follows by conditioning \(z^\top v\) on \(z^\top u\), and the second is the standard arcsine formula for the signs of two jointly Gaussian variables.
Bernstein's and Hoeffding's inequalities concentrate the corresponding empirical averages within \(\varepsilon\) with failure at most \(Ce^{-cd\varepsilon^2}\).
Finally, for either prescribed \(s\),
\[
\frac1d\#\{a:|\widetilde X_a|\le s\}\le\frac1d\#\{a:|X_a|\le s+b\}+\frac{\|\widetilde X-X\|_2^2}{db^2}\le Cs+C\varepsilon^2
\]
except with probability \(Ce^{-cd\varepsilon^4}\).
A union bound over the pairs and the two thresholds proves \eqref{eq:when2-quant-haar-statistics}; independence between different pairs is not needed.

label: lem:when2-diet-haar-recovery
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Generic common rotation restores the Row coefficient advantage

label: eq:when2-diet-haar-sign-laws
title: Proof
body_md:
The hypotheses imply \(\|\bar\mu\|_2^2\le(1+\delta_d)/k+\delta_d\le C\varepsilon^2\).
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:when2-quant-haar-sign} to the means.
The norm and coherence assumptions, together with \eqref{eq:when2-quant-haar-statistics}, give, for \(T_i=\operatorname{sign}(R\mu_i)\),
\begin{equation}
\max_i\left|\frac{\|R\mu_i\|_1}{\sqrt d}-g_0\right|+\max_{i\ne j}\frac{|T_j^\top R\mu_i|}{\sqrt d}+\max_{i\ne j}\frac{|T_i^\top T_j|}{d}\le C\varepsilon.
\label{eq:when2-diet-haar-sign-laws}
\end{equation}
Choose a fixed sufficiently large constant \(C_0\) and apply that lemma with thresholds \((C_0\varepsilon)^{1/2}\) and \((C_0\varepsilon)^{1/8}\).
After decreasing \(\varepsilon_0\), Lemma~\ref{lem:when2-quant-deterministic-rigidity} applies at precision \(C_0\varepsilon\), with \(h=g_0\).
It follows that every Row minimizer is within \(C\varepsilon^{1/4}\) per row of the rotated means, while every rescaled Max minimizer is within \(C\varepsilon^{1/16}\sqrt d\) per row of \(T_i\).

It remains to calculate the test-noise energy of the canonical sign contrast
\[
b_{ij}:=\frac{T_i-T_j}{\|T_i-T_j\|_2}.
\]
Fix a pair, let \(S=\operatorname{span}\{\mu_i,\mu_j\}\), and choose an orthonormal basis \(F\in\mathbb R^{d\times2}\) of \(S\).
The Gram matrix of the pair is uniformly well-conditioned under the assumed bound on \(\delta_d\).
Conditioning only on \(RF\), the vector \(b_{ij}\) is fixed whenever it is defined.
Set \(p=(RF)^\top b_{ij}\), \(q=Fp\), and \(r^2=1-\|p\|_2^2\).
The unexposed action of \(R\) on the orthogonal complement is Haar, so conditionally
\begin{equation}
R^\top b_{ij}=q+r\zeta,
\label{eq:when2-diet-haar-decomposition}
\end{equation}
where \(\zeta\) is uniform on the unit sphere of \(S^\perp\).
On the sign-statistics event, \eqref{eq:when2-quant-haar-statistics} gives
\[
b_{ij}^\top R\mu_i=\frac{g_0}{\sqrt2}+O(\varepsilon),\qquad b_{ij}^\top R\mu_j=-\frac{g_0}{\sqrt2}+O(\varepsilon).
\]
The same two inner products for \(g_0v_{ij}\) are \(g_0/\sqrt2+O(\delta_d)\) and \(-g_0/\sqrt2+O(\delta_d)\).
Inverting the well-conditioned two-by-two Gram matrix therefore yields
\begin{equation}
\|q-g_0v_{ij}\|_2\le C\varepsilon,\qquad |r^2-(1-g_0^2)|\le C\varepsilon.
\label{eq:when2-diet-haar-projection}
\end{equation}
For the conditional complement calculation, let \(P_S\) denote the orthogonal projector onto \(S\).
Representing \(\zeta\) by a normalized standard Gaussian in \(S^\perp\) and applying the bounded-weight quadratic-form and Gaussian linear-form bounds gives
\[
\left|\zeta^\top\Sigma\zeta-\frac{\operatorname{tr}((I_d-P_S)\Sigma)}{d-2}\right|+|q^\top\Sigma\zeta|\le C\varepsilon
\]
with conditional failure at most \(Ce^{-cd\varepsilon^2}\), uniformly in the exposed frame.
The trace ratio is \(1+O(d^{-1})\), since \(\operatorname{tr}\Sigma=d\) and \(\operatorname{rank}P_S=2\).
The conditional failure bound can be integrated and then union-bounded over pairs; we do not condition on the sign vectors of the other classes.
Combining this bound with \eqref{eq:when2-diet-haar-decomposition} and \eqref{eq:when2-diet-haar-projection} gives
\begin{equation}
\max_{i\ne j}\left|b_{ij}^\top\Sigma^\circ b_{ij}-(g_0^2a_{ij}+1-g_0^2)\right|\le C\varepsilon.
\label{eq:when2-diet-haar-energy}
\end{equation}
The canonical Row direction \(Rv_{ij}\) has directed signal \(1/\sqrt2+O(\delta_d)\) and test-noise energy exactly \(a_{ij}\).
The canonical Max direction has directed signal \(g_0/\sqrt2+O(\varepsilon)\), and
\[
\frac{g_0^2/2}{g_0^2a_{ij}+1-g_0^2}=\frac1{2a_{ij}+\pi-2}.
\]
Both canonical contrast norms are bounded away from zero after the Max contrasts are divided by \(\sqrt d\).
Normalization stability, the whole-face bounds already proved, and \(\Sigma^\circ\succeq c_\Sigma I_d\) therefore transfer these coefficients uniformly to the complete solution sets, proving \eqref{eq:when2-diet-haar-coefficients}.
The combined failure is at most \(Ck^2e^{-cd\varepsilon^6}\).

To pass to the minimum directed coefficient, put \(a_*:=\max_{i\ne j}a_{ij}\).
Then \eqref{eq:when2-diet-haar-coefficients} implies
\[
\inf_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{row}}^\circ}E_d(W;\Sigma^\circ)-\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{max}}^\circ}E_d(W;\Sigma^\circ)\ge\frac1{2a_*}-\frac1{2a_*+\pi-2}-C\varepsilon^{1/16}.
\]
Since \(a_*\le C_\Sigma\), the difference of the two displayed fractions is at least
\begin{equation}
\Delta_{\mathrm{rot}}:=\frac{\pi-2}{2C_\Sigma(2C_\Sigma+\pi-2)}>0.
\label{eq:when2-quant-rotation-gap}
\end{equation}
Choose a fixed \(\varepsilon>0\) so that \(C\varepsilon^{1/16}\le\Delta_{\mathrm{rot}}/2\).
The regularity assumptions eventually ensure \(\delta_d+d^{-1}+k^{-1}\le\varepsilon^2\).
Lemma~\ref{lem:when2-diet-error-transfer} gives the strict accuracy ordering, and absorbing \(k^2\) into the exponential proves \eqref{eq:when2-diet-haar-row-win}.

\]
Then \(2\bar\gamma_{1/2}^2\bar\gamma_2/\pi>1\), and hence the transition point in Proposition~\ref{prop:main-coordinate-reversal} lies in \((0,1)\).
In particular, the transition condition does not require a special spectral shape: within a fixed bounded spectral range, the displayed lower bound on the limiting spectral variance is sufficient.

title: Proof
body_md:
Concavity of \(x\mapsto\sqrt{x}\) places its graph above the chord joining \((\underline\gamma,\sqrt{\underline\gamma})\) and \((\overline\gamma,\sqrt{\overline\gamma})\).
Averaging this chord inequality and using \(d^{-1}\sum_a\gamma_{a,d}=1\) gives \(\bar\gamma_{1/2}\ge q_*\).
Trace normalization also gives \(\bar\gamma_2=1+v_\Gamma\), and therefore
\[
\frac{2\bar\gamma_{1/2}^2\bar\gamma_2}{\pi}\ge\frac{2q_*^2(1+v_\Gamma)}{\pi}>1.
\]

title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:app-coordinate-dispersion-nonvacuous}
Write \(l:=\underline\gamma\) and \(u:=\overline\gamma\).
The variance permitted by the spectral range is itself bounded.
Indeed, since \(l\le\gamma_{a,d}\le u\), we have \((\gamma_{a,d}-l)(u-\gamma_{a,d})\ge0\), or equivalently \(\gamma_{a,d}^2\le(l+u)\gamma_{a,d}-lu\).
Averaging and using the trace normalization \(d^{-1}\sum_a\gamma_{a,d}=1\) gives \(\bar\gamma_2\le l+u-lu\), and hence \(v_\Gamma=\bar\gamma_2-1\le(1-l)(u-1)\).
This bound is sharp: it is attained asymptotically by a two-point spectral profile supported on \(l\) and \(u\) with respective masses \((u-1)/(u-l)\) and \((1-l)/(u-l)\).

Consequently, the dispersion condition in Corollary~\ref{cor:app-coordinate-dispersed-profiles} is non-vacuous if and only if \((1-l)(u-1)>\pi/(2q_*^2)-1\).
Using \(q_*=(1+\sqrt{lu})/(\sqrt l+\sqrt u)\), this is equivalently
\[
\frac{2(1+\sqrt{lu})^2(l+u-lu)}{\pi(\sqrt l+\sqrt u)^2}>1.
\]
For each fixed \(l\in(0,1)\), the left-hand side is strictly increasing in \(u>1\), so there is a unique critical value \(u_c(l)>1\) above which the sufficient dispersion condition can be satisfied.

title: Setup
body_md: The main-text experiment in Figure~\ref{fig:experiments} (left) uses \(k=60\) classes and dimension \(d=20\). For each class \(i\), we draw \(\mu_i\sim\mathcal N({\mathbf 0},I_d/d)\), draw the number of training examples independently and uniformly from \(\{1,\ldots,5\}\), and generate \(x_{i,r}^{\mathrm{tr}}=\mu_i+0.2236\,\varepsilon_{i,r}^{\mathrm{tr}}\) and \(x_{i,r}^{\mathrm{te}}=\mu_i+2.2361\,\varepsilon_{i,r}^{\mathrm{te}}\), where all residual vectors are independent \(\mathcal N({\mathbf 0},I_d/d)\). Test-class proportions are drawn independently from \(\operatorname{Dirichlet}(\mathbf 1_k)\), and each of the 30 paired seeds uses \(120{,}000\) evaluation examples. All methods within a seed use the same training and evaluation data.
